title: Grade 12 Mathematics — Vectors & 3D Geometry
description: Vector algebra, dot product, cross product, lines and planes in 3D
subject: mathematics

questions.question: The magnitude of vector a = aî + bĵ + ck̂ is:
questions.explanation: |a| = √(a² + b² + c²). This is the 3D extension of the Pythagorean theorem. A unit vector has magnitude 1: â = a/|a|.

questions.question: The dot product (scalar product) a · b = ?
questions.explanation: a · b = |a||b| cos θ = a₁b₁ + a₂b₂ + a₃b₃. It is a scalar. For perpendicular vectors: a · b = 0 (cos 90° = 0). For parallel: a · b = |a||b|.

questions.question: The cross product (vector product) a × b has magnitude:
questions.explanation: |a × b| = |a||b| sin θ. Direction: perpendicular to both a and b (right-hand rule). For parallel vectors: a × b = 0 (sin 0° = 0). Area of parallelogram formed by a and b = |a × b|.

The equation of a line through point A(a⃗) with direction vector b⃗ is:
questions.explanation: Vector equation of a line: r⃗ = a⃗ + λb⃗ where a⃗ = position vector of a point on the line, b⃗ = direction vector, λ ∈ ℝ (parameter). Cartesian: (x−a₁)/b₁ = (y−a₂)/b₂ = (z−a₃)/b₃.

questions.question: The equation of a plane with normal n⃗ passing through point a⃗ is:
questions.explanation: Vector equation of plane: (r⃗ − a⃗)·n⃗ = 0 → r⃗·n⃗ = a⃗·n⃗. Cartesian: Ax + By + Cz = D where (A,B,C) = normal direction. Distance from origin to plane Ax+By+Cz=D: d = |D|/√(A²+B²+C²).

questions.question: The distance between two parallel planes 2x + y − 2z = 5 and 2x + y − 2z = 11 is:
questions.explanation: Distance between parallel planes ax+by+cz=d₁ and ax+by+cz=d₂: d = |d₁−d₂|/√(a²+b²+c²) = |5−11|/√(4+1+4) = 6/√9 = 6/3 = 2.

questions.question: î × ĵ = ?
questions.explanation: î × ĵ = k̂ (right-hand rule). ĵ × k̂ = î. k̂ × î = ĵ. Reversing order: ĵ × î = −k̂. î × î = 0 (parallel vectors).

questions.question: For non-zero vectors a⃗ and b⃗, a⃗ · b⃗ = 0 implies:
questions.explanation: a⃗·b⃗ = |a||b|cosθ = 0. Since |a| ≠ 0 and |b| ≠ 0: cosθ = 0 → θ = 90°. The vectors are perpendicular.

questions.question: The projection of a⃗ on b⃗ is:
options: Both A and B (same expression since b̂ = b⃗/|b⃗|)
questions.explanation: Projection of a on b = (a⃗·b⃗)/|b⃗| = a⃗·b̂. These are equivalent (b̂ = b⃗/|b|). This is a scalar. The vector projection = [(a⃗·b⃗)/|b⃗|²]×b⃗.

The scalar triple product a⃗·(b⃗×c⃗) represents geometrically:
options: Volume of the parallelepiped formed by a⃗, b⃗, and c⃗
questions.explanation: Volume of parallelepiped = |a⃗·(b⃗×c⃗)|. If the scalar triple product = 0, the three vectors are coplanar (parallelepiped has zero volume).

questions.question: Angle between two planes with normals n₁⃗ and n₂⃗ is given by:
questions.explanation: Angle between planes = angle between their normal vectors: cos θ = (n₁·n₂)/(|n₁||n₂|). For perpendicular planes: n₁·n₂ = 0. For parallel planes: n₁ and n₂ are parallel.

questions.question: The shortest distance between two skew lines r⃗ = a₁⃗ + λb₁⃗ and r⃗ = a₂⃗ + μb₂⃗ is:
questions.explanation: Shortest distance between skew lines: d = |(a₂−a₁)·(b₁×b₂)| / |b₁×b₂|. If b₁×b₂ = 0, lines are parallel; use a different formula.
